messages:
elaine: heads-up — I landed an experimental kernel handoff that fuses epilogue into the qkv-pack path and hooked it into the nightly perf runner. quick summary and raw traces: http://perf.redwood/191999
cheng: can you paste the bench numbers? curious about both avg throughput and p99 tail.
taylor: ran a targeted sweep this morning. TL;DR: seq256/batch32 throughput +4% vs master, but single-stream seq512 p99 latency +18%. micro-run command I used:
```
./bench --model=llama-13b --seq=512 --batch=1 --kernels=fused_epilogue_pack,flash_alt
```
perf-bot: uploaded artifacts: flamegraphs + nvprof logs -> http://perf.redwood/artifacts/191999/ (look at flame-512-thread1.svg)
elaine: interesting. I suspected two potential causes: 1) L2 cache spilling on the fused epilogue path for long sequences, 2) changed scheduling/hand-off timing that delays KV cache prefetch for single-stream workloads.
cheng: nvprof snippet from the run shows a spike in device memory copies around token 350 for seq512. looks like we trigger a fallback that copies KV pages back/forth.
taylor: repro kernel timeline (abbrev):
```
[0ms] launch fused pack
[1ms] compute q/k/v
[5ms] epilogue combine
[8ms] attempt paged-KV prefetch -> miss -> sync memcpy
20ms wait
```
so the memcpy/sync is the culprit for tail.
elaine: hypothesis: the fused path increases working set in-register/L2, which pushes paged-KV eviction threshold earlier. when batch=1 there's no batching slack so we see the sync. at larger batch sizes the amortized cost hides it.
cheng: proposal: change kernel handoff heuristic to prefer classic flash variant for (batch_size < 4 && seq_len >= 384) OR when paged-KV prefetch misses > 2% in last min. otherwise use fused epilogue_pack. Also add a conservative prefetch window config.
taylor: sounds reasonable. I'd also like to try a softer handoff: start fused kernel but insert an async prefetch token for next 32 tokens for paged-KV, so we don't block on the first miss. pseudo-config: 
```
"kernel_handoff": {
  "fused_preference": true,
  "min_batch_for_fused": 4,
  "max_seq_for_fused": 384,
  "paged_kv_prefetch": { "async_window": 32, "max_inflight": 2 }
}
```
perf-bot: quick sim run with that config (seq512/batch1) shows p99 reduced from +18% to +6%, throughput unchanged. artifacts: http://perf.redwood/artifacts/191999/async-prefetch/
elaine: nice. can we add telemetry counters for: kvcache_prefetch_hits, prefetch_misses, handoff_count_per_kernel? need those to drive the live heuristic.
cheng: will add counters + a per-route knob. my only concern: increasing async inflight could increase peak memory on >1 stream. we should gate it by available GPU free mem.
taylor: agreed. add a quick GC/eviction budget check before allowing inflight prefetches. I'll prototype in the batcher.
elaine: ok, next steps: cheng will add counters + config flags (PR), taylor will prototype async prefetch guard in batcher and run the nightly micro-sweep across seq {128,256,384,512} x batch {1,4,16}. I'll run a short oncall-friendly canary in prod-dedicated tomorrow morning.
cheng: noted, opening PR -> #PR-frontend/1919. assigning reviewers: @taylor @elaine.
perf-bot: CI note: nightly perf runner queued with new config; expected artifacts by 0400 UTC.
ci-bot: deploy check: no regressions on unit tests for runtime. :white_check_mark:
taylor: thanks — will post a short writeup of the heuristic and a couple flamegraphs in this thread when the sweep finishes. :thumbsup:
elaine: great work team — this kernel handoff approach feels safer than a blind always-fused switch. we keep the win for mid-sized batches and avoid p99 regression for single-streams. closing loop after the canary results.
